assumptions: Costs, the tariff and any funding are your own figures, labelled your estimate, not sourced or reviewed market prices.
Amounts are never converted between currencies; a different currency is reported, not applied.
No future inflation or price change is assumed; annual figures are flat and spread over 365 days.
A contingency you set is added to the cost estimates; it is not an invented margin.
Only water that replaces tanker deliveries is valued; water beyond the tanker deliveries it could replace earns nothing here.

needs: Greywater reuse: tell us whether there is space for a tank.
Leak detection and repair: estimate share of piped supply lost to leaks, share of those losses the repairs stop, a build time (you set a time limit or horizon).
Metering and demand awareness: estimate share of water use saved by metering and feedback, a build time (you set a time limit or horizon).
Rooftop rainwater harvesting for use: tell us the roof area you can collect from.
Additional storage: tell us whether there is space for a tank.
assumptions: Average day: water saved or added replaces tanker deliveries first; water beyond the tanker deliveries is not counted.
Demand savings multiply; greywater replaces only the demand left after them.
Rainfall is spread evenly over the year; a tank's size and dry months are not modelled, so harvested water is an average, not a guarantee in dry weeks.
Measures in one option are assumed to be built at the same time.
comparison.ranking: Fewest measures, then the largest margin past the target at pessimistic estimates, then measure ids.
